title: BJT Current Mirror: How Q2 Copies Q1's Current
topic: Two matched NPN transistors share a base-emitter voltage. The left branch (Q1 diode-connected with a reference resistor) sets V_BE; the right branch (Q2 with its base tied to Q1's) copies that V_BE, so its collector current mirrors the reference current. A swept reference drives both branches and the right-side readout tracks the left in lockstep.

beats.narration: How do you copy a current from one branch of a chip to another, without measuring it?

elements.content: Two transistors. One reference. One copy.

beats.narration: Two matched NPN transistors share their bases and emitters. Q one is diode connected — its collector ties back to its base — and a reference resistor sets the current that flows through it.

beats.narration: Both transistors see the same V B E. Because collector current depends only on V B E, the two collector currents are equal — Q two simply copies the current set by R reference.

beats.narration: Change R reference and I reference moves. I out tracks it in lockstep — that's the mirror in action.
